symptoms.name: Fever
symptoms.description: Fever is a regulated elevation of body temperature above the individual's normal range, produced when pyrogens reset the hypothalamic thermoregulatory set point. It is most often a response to infection but also accompanies inflammatory, malignant, drug-related and other conditions.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Fever accompanies a very wide range of infectious and non-infectious illnesses and narrows the differential little on its own.
causes: Bacterial infections (e.g., pneumonia, urinary tract infection, typhoid fever)
red_flags: Confusion or reduced level of consciousness
Petechial or purpuric rash, or mucosal bleeding

symptoms.name: Chills / rigors
symptoms.description: Chills are a sensation of coldness, often with shivering and pallor, that occur as body temperature rises toward a newly elevated set point. Rigors are intense, uncontrollable shaking chills ('teeth-chattering, bed-shaking') that are associated with rapid temperature rise and suggest bacteremia or other acute infection.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Chills accompany most febrile illnesses, although true rigors modestly favour bacteremia, malaria, pyelonephritis and similar infections.
red_flags: Hypotension or cold, mottled extremities (possible sepsis)
Rapid breathing or low oxygen saturation
Rigors after travel to a malaria-endemic area

symptoms.name: Headache
symptoms.description: Headache is pain in any region of the head, arising from pain-sensitive intracranial or extracranial structures. Most headaches are primary (migraine, tension-type, cluster), but headache also accompanies systemic infection and can signal serious intracranial disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Headache is extremely common and accompanies many primary headache disorders and systemic illnesses, so it has low specificity alone.
causes: Systemic viral or bacterial infection (e.g., influenza, dengue)
Meningitis or intracranial hemorrhage (less common, serious)
red_flags: Focal neurological deficits, confusion or slurred speech
New headache after age 50 or after head injury

Headache. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Retro-orbital pain (pain behind the eyes)
symptoms.description: Retro-orbital pain is aching or pressure felt behind the eyeball, often worsened by eye movement. In febrile illness it is a characteristic feature of dengue, accompanying severe headache, myalgia and arthralgia; it also occurs with migraine, sinusitis and orbital disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: In a febrile patient, pain behind the eyes points fairly strongly toward dengue and other arboviral infections.
red_flags: Red, painful eye with reduced vision
In dengue: abdominal pain, persistent vomiting or mucosal bleeding
Proptosis or fever with swollen eyelids

Eye pain. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Muscle aches (myalgia)
symptoms.description: Myalgia is diffuse or localized pain in skeletal muscles, which may also be felt in the associated tendons, ligaments and fascia. Generalized myalgia is a common feature of systemic viral and bacterial infections, while localized myalgia more often reflects overuse or injury.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Generalized muscle aches accompany many infections and systemic illnesses and are only weakly discriminating.
red_flags: Fever with jaundice or reduced urine output
Severe pain with swelling of a limb

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Muscle aches. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Calf muscle pain / tenderness
symptoms.description: Calf pain is pain or tenderness localized to the posterior lower leg muscles. In an acute febrile illness, myalgia characteristically involving the calves and lower back is a recognized feature of leptospirosis; outside that context, calf pain is often musculoskeletal or vascular.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Febrile illness with prominent calf muscle pain is a classic pointer toward leptospirosis, especially after flood or animal-urine exposure.
red_flags: Unilateral calf swelling, warmth or redness (possible deep vein thrombosis)
Fever with jaundice, reduced urine output or bleeding

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking

Leptospirosis. CDC Yellow Book: Health Information for International Travel. Atlanta (GA): Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
Leg pain. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Joint pain (arthralgia)
symptoms.description: Arthralgia is pain in one or more joints without necessarily visible swelling or inflammation. It may arise from injury, degenerative or inflammatory arthritis, or as part of systemic infection such as dengue ('breakbone fever').
symptoms.weight_rationale: Joint pain is common in systemic infection and rheumatic disease; its pattern and accompanying features determine how much it narrows the differential.
causes: Rheumatoid arthritis and other inflammatory arthritides
red_flags: Single hot, swollen joint with fever (possible septic arthritis)
Joint pain with rash and bleeding
Rapid onset of multiple swollen joints

symptoms.name: Skin rash
symptoms.description: A rash is a change in the colour, texture or feel of the skin, which may be macular, papular, vesicular, petechial or urticarial. In febrile illness, a generalized exanthem accompanies many viral infections (e.g., measles, dengue) and some bacterial and drug-related conditions.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Rash is shared by many infections and drug reactions, but its morphology and distribution add useful discriminating information.
red_flags: Petechial or purpuric rash that does not blanch
Rash with fever and low blood pressure
Rash with facial or throat swelling or difficulty breathing

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking

symptoms.name: Mucosal bleeding / petechiae (gum bleeding, nosebleed)
symptoms.description: Mucocutaneous bleeding includes petechiae (pinpoint red dots from capillary bleeding), bruising, nosebleeds (epistaxis) and gum bleeding. In dengue, minor mucocutaneous bleeding may occur, and mucosal bleeding is listed as a warning sign of severe dengue; it also reflects thrombocytopenia or coagulation disorders.
symptoms.weight_rationale: In an acute febrile illness, spontaneous mucosal bleeding or petechiae strongly suggests dengue or another cause of thrombocytopenia or coagulopathy.
causes: Leukemia and other bone marrow disorders
Local causes (dry nasal mucosa, gingivitis) for isolated nosebleed or gum bleeding
red_flags: Persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain or lethargy in dengue
Signs of shock (cold extremities, weak pulse)
Widespread new petechiae or bruising with fever

Bleeding into the skin. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Abdominal pain
symptoms.description: Abdominal pain is pain felt anywhere between the chest and the groin, arising from abdominal organs, the abdominal wall or referred from outside the abdomen. Its location, character, timing and associated features guide the differential, and severity does not always reflect seriousness.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Abdominal pain without localisation is common to many gastrointestinal, urinary, gynecological and systemic conditions.
causes: Urinary tract infection or kidney stones
red_flags: Sudden, severe pain or rigid abdomen
Vomiting blood or passing bloody or black stools
Pain with fever and inability to pass stool
Pain with chest, neck or shoulder pain, or difficulty breathing

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking

symptoms.name: Epigastric pain
symptoms.description: Epigastric pain is pain or burning located in the upper central abdomen below the xiphoid process. It is characteristic of peptic ulcer disease, gastritis and functional dyspepsia, but cardiac, biliary and pancreatic disease may also present here.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Pain localised to the epigastrium focuses the differential on upper gastrointestinal causes, while still overlapping with cardiac and pancreaticobiliary disease.
red_flags: Vomiting blood or black, tarry stools
Unintentional weight loss or difficulty swallowing
Pain with sweating or breathlessness (possible cardiac cause)
Sudden severe pain with rigid abdomen (possible perforation)

Abdominal pain. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Heartburn
symptoms.description: Heartburn is a painful burning feeling just below or behind the breastbone, usually caused by reflux of gastric acid into the esophagus. It is often worse after meals, when lying down or bending over.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Retrosternal burning related to meals and posture is fairly characteristic of acid reflux and peptic disease.
causes: Large or fatty meals, alcohol, smoking
red_flags: Chest pain with sweating, breathlessness or radiation to the arm or jaw (possible cardiac cause)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking

Heartburn. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Nausea & vomiting
symptoms.description: Nausea is an unpleasant sensation of the urge to vomit, and vomiting (emesis) is forceful expulsion of gastric contents through the mouth. Both are common and arise from gastrointestinal, central nervous system, metabolic, drug-related and pregnancy-related causes.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Nausea and vomiting occur in a very wide range of gastrointestinal and systemic conditions and are nonspecific alone.
causes: Raised intracranial pressure or other central causes
red_flags: Blood or coffee-ground material in the vomit
Signs of dehydration (no urine for 8 hours, dry mouth, sunken eyes)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Nausea and vomiting - adults. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Diarrhea
symptoms.description: Diarrhea is the passage of loose or watery stools, typically three or more times a day. Acute diarrhea is most often infectious, while chronic diarrhea suggests malabsorptive, inflammatory or functional disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Diarrhea points toward intestinal involvement, most often acute infectious gastroenteritis, but also occurs in systemic infections.
red_flags: Blood or pus in the stool
Signs of dehydration or reduced urine output
Diarrhea lasting more than several days

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Diarrhea. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Constipation
symptoms.description: Constipation is infrequent bowel movements (commonly fewer than three per week) or hard, dry stools that are difficult or painful to pass. It is most often functional or dietary, but may reflect medicines, metabolic disease or bowel obstruction.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Constipation is common and usually functional, adding limited diagnostic information on its own.
causes: Low dietary fibre or fluid intake
red_flags: Inability to pass stool or gas with vomiting and abdominal distension
New change in bowel habit in older adults

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Constipation. MedlinePlus Health Topics. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Black, tarry stools (melena)
symptoms.description: Melena is the passage of black, sticky, tarry stools with a characteristic foul odour, produced when blood from the upper gastrointestinal tract is digested. It usually indicates bleeding from the esophagus, stomach or duodenum; iron and bismuth can blacken stools but do not make them tarry.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Tarry black stool localises bleeding to the upper gastrointestinal tract, most commonly peptic ulcer disease.
red_flags: Rapid heart rate or low blood pressure
Use of anticoagulants or antiplatelet agents

Black or tarry stools. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Vomiting blood (hematemesis)
symptoms.description: Hematemesis is vomiting of fresh blood, clots or dark 'coffee-ground' material from the upper gastrointestinal tract. It indicates bleeding proximal to the ligament of Treitz and requires assessment for hemodynamic instability.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Vomiting blood localises bleeding to the upper gastrointestinal tract and is a strong pointer toward peptic ulcer, varices or mucosal tears.
red_flags: Rapid heart rate or low blood pressure

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.

Vomiting blood. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Loss of appetite
symptoms.description: Loss of appetite is a reduced desire to eat; the medical term is anorexia (distinct from the eating disorder anorexia nervosa). It accompanies many acute infections as well as chronic, malignant, psychiatric and medicine-related conditions.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Reduced appetite is a highly nonspecific accompaniment of many acute and chronic illnesses.
causes: Chronic liver, kidney or heart disease
red_flags: Persistent loss of appetite with night sweats or fever

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Appetite - decreased. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Fatigue & malaise
symptoms.description: Fatigue is a feeling of weariness, tiredness or lack of energy that is not relieved by usual rest, and malaise is a general sense of being unwell. Both accompany a very broad range of infectious, metabolic, hematologic, psychiatric and lifestyle-related conditions.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Fatigue and malaise are among the least specific symptoms and occur in most acute and chronic illnesses.
causes: Heart failure and chronic kidney disease
red_flags: Fatigue with breathlessness or chest pain
Unintentional weight loss or night sweats
Fatigue with bleeding, pallor or jaundice

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Fatigue. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Unintentional weight loss
symptoms.description: Unintentional weight loss is a decrease in body weight that occurs without deliberate dieting or exercise. Clinically significant loss (commonly defined as more than 5% of body weight over 6-12 months) warrants evaluation for malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine and gastrointestinal disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Unintentional weight loss narrows the differential toward chronic infection, malignancy and endocrine disease but remains broad.

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Weight loss - unintentional. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Night sweats
symptoms.description: Night sweats are episodes of sweating during sleep severe enough to soak nightclothes or bedding, resulting from exaggeration of the normal circadian temperature rhythm. They may accompany any febrile illness and are classically associated with tuberculosis and lymphoma.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Drenching night sweats, especially with weight loss or chronic cough, direct attention toward tuberculosis, lymphoma and other chronic infections.
causes: Other chronic infections (e.g., lung abscess, endocarditis, brucellosis)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.

symptoms.name: Cough
symptoms.description: Cough is a protective reflex that expels air forcefully to clear the airways of secretions and irritants. It is classified as acute (under 3 weeks), subacute (3-8 weeks) or chronic (over 8 weeks) and may be dry or productive.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Cough is common to most respiratory infections and many airway diseases and discriminates poorly alone.
red_flags: Shortness of breath or chest pain
Cough lasting more than 3 weeks with weight loss or night sweats

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Cough. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Productive cough (sputum)
symptoms.description: A productive cough brings up sputum from the lower respiratory tract. Purulent sputum (yellow, green, opaque) suggests bacterial infection, rust-coloured sputum is associated with pneumococcal pneumonia, and pink frothy sputum suggests pulmonary edema.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Sputum production points to lower respiratory tract involvement, and its character (purulent, rusty, blood-streaked) adds diagnostic value.
red_flags: Shortness of breath or low oxygen saturation
High fever with pleuritic chest pain
Chronic cough with weight loss and night sweats

Cough. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Coughing up blood (hemoptysis)
symptoms.description: Hemoptysis is the expectoration of blood or blood-tinged sputum originating from the lungs or tracheobronchial tree, distinguished from bleeding from the nose, mouth or upper gastrointestinal tract. Massive hemoptysis is a life-threatening emergency.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Coughing up blood narrows the differential to a limited set of pulmonary causes, prominently tuberculosis, bronchitis, bronchiectasis, lung cancer and pulmonary embolism.
red_flags: Shortness of breath or low oxygen saturation
Low blood pressure or rapid heart rate

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Corey R. Hemoptysis. In: Walker HK, Hall WD, Hurst JW, editors. Clinical Methods: The History, Physical, and Laboratory Examinations. 3rd ed. Boston: Butterworths; 1990.
Coughing up blood. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Shortness of breath (dyspnea)
symptoms.description: Dyspnea is a subjective sensation of uncomfortable or difficult breathing, or of not getting enough air. It arises from respiratory, cardiac, metabolic, hematologic and psychological causes, and severe or sudden dyspnea can indicate a life-threatening condition.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Breathlessness points to cardiopulmonary disease but is shared by many respiratory, cardiac and systemic conditions.
red_flags: Blue lips or low oxygen saturation

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Breathing difficulty. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Suha F, Modi P, Sharma S. Dyspnea. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Wheezing
symptoms.description: Wheezing is a high-pitched, musical sound produced by airflow through narrowed or compressed airways, usually most prominent on expiration. It is characteristic of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, but 'all that wheezes is not asthma'.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Wheeze indicates airway narrowing and strongly favours obstructive airway diseases such as asthma and COPD.
red_flags: Difficulty speaking or use of accessory muscles
Blue lips or low oxygen saturation
Wheeze that is unilateral or fixed (possible obstruction)
Silent chest in a patient with severe asthma

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Wheezing. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Gong H Jr. Wheezing and Asthma. In: Walker HK, Hall WD, Hurst JW, editors. Clinical Methods: The History, Physical, and Laboratory Examinations. 3rd ed. Boston: Butterworths; 1990.

symptoms.name: Chest tightness
symptoms.description: Chest tightness is a sensation of constriction or inability to fully expand the chest. It is one of the cardinal symptoms of asthma, often reported more frequently than wheeze, but a sensation of tightness or pressure may also represent myocardial ischemia.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Chest tightness with wheeze or cough favours bronchospasm, although overlap with cardiac ischemic pain limits specificity.
red_flags: Tightness with sweating, nausea or radiation to arm or jaw
Inability to speak in full sentences
Symptoms not relieved by usual reliever inhaler

symptoms.name: Pleuritic chest pain
symptoms.description: Pleuritic chest pain is sharp, localized pain in the chest, neck or shoulder that worsens with breathing, coughing or sneezing. It results from irritation or inflammation of the parietal pleura; pulmonary embolism is the most frequent serious cause.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Pain that is sharp and worsened by breathing localises the process to the pleura and narrows the differential to pleural, pulmonary and pericardial causes.
red_flags: Sudden onset with shortness of breath (possible embolism or pneumothorax)
Low blood pressure or low oxygen saturation

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Hunter MP, Goldin J, Regunath H. Pleurisy. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Chest pain or pressure (angina-like)
symptoms.description: Anginal chest pain is typically a dull, heavy, pressing or crushing substernal discomfort that may radiate to the arm, neck or jaw, is precipitated by exertion or stress and relieved by rest. Chest pain has a broad differential that includes several immediately life-threatening causes.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Pressure-like substernal pain with exertional features points toward myocardial ischemia, though other thoracic causes overlap.
red_flags: Pain lasting more than a few minutes at rest
Radiation to arm, jaw, neck or back
Sudden tearing pain radiating to the back

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Chest pain. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Johnson K, Ghassemzadeh S. Chest Pain. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Sore throat
symptoms.description: Sore throat is discomfort, pain or scratchiness in the throat that often makes swallowing painful. Most cases are due to viral upper respiratory infection; group A streptococcus is the main bacterial cause.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Sore throat localises disease to the upper respiratory tract but is shared by many viral and bacterial infections.
causes: Viral upper respiratory infections (common cold, influenza, COVID-19)
red_flags: Inability to swallow or open the mouth
Muffled voice or one-sided throat swelling (possible abscess)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Pharyngitis - sore throat. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Runny nose (coryza)
symptoms.description: Rhinorrhea is discharge of fluid from the nose, often with nasal congestion, caused by inflamed nasal mucosa and blood vessels. Coryza (runny nose with sneezing and congestion) is typical of viral upper respiratory infections and is part of the measles prodrome.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Runny nose points to the upper respiratory tract but is common to colds, influenza, allergy and measles.
causes: Common cold and other viral upper respiratory infections
red_flags: High fever with conjunctivitis and cough (possible measles)
Clear watery discharge after head injury
Facial swelling or severe facial pain

Stuffy or runny nose - adult. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Red eyes (conjunctivitis / conjunctival suffusion)
symptoms.description: Red eye results from dilated or swollen blood vessels on the surface of the eye. Conjunctivitis involves inflammation with discharge, whereas conjunctival suffusion is redness without purulent discharge that is characteristic of leptospirosis; conjunctivitis is also part of the measles prodrome.
symptoms.weight_rationale: In a febrile patient, conjunctival suffusion or conjunctivitis points toward leptospirosis or measles.
red_flags: Severe headache with nausea (possible acute glaucoma)
Fever with jaundice or reduced urine output (possible severe leptospirosis)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Eye redness. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Leptospirosis. CDC Yellow Book: Health Information for International Travel. Atlanta (GA): Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

symptoms.name: Koplik spots
symptoms.description: Koplik spots are small bluish-white spots, about 2-3 mm, on an erythematous base on the buccal mucosa opposite the molars, likened to 'grains of salt on a red background'. They typically appear about a day before the measles rash and fade as the rash develops.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Koplik spots are considered pathognomonic of measles, so their presence strongly confirms the diagnosis.
red_flags: Dehydration from diarrhea or poor intake

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Jain P, Rathee M. Koplik Spots. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.
Measles. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Loss of smell or taste
symptoms.description: Anosmia is partial or total loss of the sense of smell, and ageusia or dysgeusia refers to loss or distortion of taste; because flavour depends largely on smell, the two are often reported together. Sudden loss of smell is a recognised feature of viral upper respiratory infections, notably COVID-19.
symptoms.weight_rationale: New, sudden loss of smell or taste during an acute respiratory illness is relatively characteristic of COVID-19.
causes: Common cold and other viral upper respiratory infections
red_flags: Loss of smell with other neurological symptoms
Loss of smell after head injury
Persistent one-sided nasal obstruction or bleeding

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Smell - impaired. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Taste - impaired. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Jaundice
symptoms.description: Jaundice is yellow discolouration of the skin, mucous membranes and sclerae caused by accumulation of bilirubin. Scleral icterus is best appreciated when serum bilirubin exceeds about 3 mg/dL, and causes are grouped as prehepatic, hepatic and posthepatic.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Jaundice localises the problem to hemolysis, liver disease or biliary obstruction, and in febrile illness points toward hepatitis, leptospirosis or severe malaria.
red_flags: Fever with right upper abdominal pain

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Jaundice. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Joseph A, Samant H. Jaundice. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Dark urine
symptoms.description: Dark urine is urine that is dark yellow, tea- or cola-coloured. Dark brown clear urine may reflect bilirubinuria from liver disease, while dark urine can also result from severe dehydration, rhabdomyolysis, hemoglobinuria, blood in the urine or certain foods and medicines.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Tea- or cola-coloured urine narrows the differential to liver disease, hemolysis, rhabdomyolysis or hematuria.

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Urine - abnormal color. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Decreased urine output (oliguria)
symptoms.description: Oliguria is reduced urine output, commonly defined in adults as less than 400 mL per day (or below about 0.5 mL/kg/h). Causes are classified as prerenal (reduced kidney perfusion, e.g., dehydration or shock), intrinsic renal and postrenal (urinary obstruction).
symptoms.weight_rationale: Reduced urine output points to hypovolemia, shock or acute kidney injury rather than to a specific disease.
causes: Acute kidney injury (e.g., leptospirosis, severe malaria)
red_flags: No urine for 8 hours or more
Dizziness, low blood pressure or rapid pulse
Swelling or breathlessness from fluid overload

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Urine output - decreased. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Haider MZ, Aslam A. Oliguria. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Painful urination (dysuria)
symptoms.description: Dysuria is pain, burning, stinging or itching of the urethra or urethral meatus during urination. Acute cystitis is the most common cause, but urethritis, sexually transmitted infections, vaginitis and prostatitis also cause it.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Dysuria localises disease to the lower urinary or genital tract and strongly favours urinary tract infection.
red_flags: Fever, chills or flank pain (possible pyelonephritis)
Symptoms in men or with recurrent infections

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Mehta P, Leslie SW, Reddivari AKR. Dysuria. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.
Urination - painful. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Urinary frequency & urgency
symptoms.description: Urinary frequency is the need to urinate more often than usual, and urgency is a sudden, strong need to urinate. Together they are typical of bladder irritation from infection, but also occur with overactive bladder, prostatic enlargement, pregnancy and diabetes.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Frequency with urgency points to the lower urinary tract, most often cystitis, but overlaps with polyuric states.

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Frequent or urgent urination. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Flank pain
symptoms.description: Flank pain is pain in one side of the body between the upper abdomen and the back. It commonly arises from the kidney or ureter, as in pyelonephritis or kidney stones, and costovertebral angle tenderness may be present.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Flank pain localises the process to the kidney or ureter, especially with urinary symptoms or fever.
red_flags: Vomiting with inability to keep fluids down
Low blood pressure or confusion (possible urosepsis)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Flank pain. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.
Gill R, Leslie SW, Minter DA. Acute Cystitis. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Suprapubic pain
symptoms.description: Suprapubic pain is discomfort in the lower midline abdomen above the pubic bone, over the bladder. It is a typical feature of acute cystitis, and suprapubic tenderness may be found on examination.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Suprapubic pain with dysuria and frequency points strongly to lower urinary tract infection.
red_flags: Inability to pass urine with a distended bladder

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Gill R, Leslie SW, Minter DA. Acute Cystitis. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.

symptoms.name: Excessive urination (polyuria)
symptoms.description: Polyuria is production of abnormally large volumes of urine, generally more than 2.5 L per day in adults, distinct from frequent passage of small volumes. It results from osmotic diuresis (e.g., hyperglycemia), excess fluid intake, diuretics or impaired urine concentration.
symptoms.weight_rationale: True polyuria, especially with thirst, points to hyperglycemia or other disorders of water balance.
red_flags: Confusion, drowsiness or vomiting (possible hyperglycemic emergency)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Urination - excessive amount. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Excessive thirst (polydipsia)
symptoms.description: Polydipsia is an abnormal, persistent feeling of needing to drink fluids. It usually accompanies polyuria and dehydration, and is a classic symptom of uncontrolled diabetes mellitus.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Excessive thirst with polyuria is a classic pointer to hyperglycemia and other water-balance disorders.
red_flags: Vomiting or abdominal pain with rapid breathing
Blurred vision with high blood glucose

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Thirst - excessive. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Blurred vision
symptoms.description: Blurred vision is loss of sharpness of vision and inability to see fine details. It may result from refractive errors, lens changes from high blood glucose, cataract, retinal or optic nerve disease, and neurological causes.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Blurred vision is shared by ocular, metabolic and neurological disorders and discriminates moderately.
red_flags: Double vision, facial droop, weakness or speech difficulty
Severe headache with very high blood pressure

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Vision problems. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Palpitations
symptoms.description: Palpitations are an awareness of the heartbeat as pounding, racing, fluttering or irregular, felt in the chest, throat or neck. They may be benign or reflect arrhythmia, structural heart disease, anemia, thyrotoxicosis or stimulant use.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Palpitations point to the heart rhythm but have many benign and systemic causes.
red_flags: Very fast heart rate at rest

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Heart palpitations. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Breathlessness lying flat (orthopnea)
symptoms.description: Orthopnea is breathlessness in the recumbent position that is relieved by sitting or standing, often quantified by the number of pillows needed to sleep. It is characteristic of left ventricular failure due to redistribution of fluid into the pulmonary circulation, and often occurs with paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Orthopnea is a relatively specific symptom of heart failure with raised pulmonary venous pressure.

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.

Mukerji V. Dyspnea, Orthopnea, and Paroxysmal Nocturnal Dyspnea. In: Walker HK, Hall WD, Hurst JW, editors. Clinical Methods: The History, Physical, and Laboratory Examinations. 3rd ed. Boston: Butterworths; 1990.

symptoms.name: Leg swelling (edema)
symptoms.description: Peripheral edema is abnormal buildup of fluid in the tissues of the feet, ankles and legs, typically pitting on pressure. Bilateral edema suggests systemic causes such as heart, kidney or liver disease or medicines, while unilateral swelling suggests local venous or lymphatic causes.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Leg edema is shared by cardiac, renal, hepatic, venous and drug-related causes, though distribution helps narrow it.
red_flags: Shortness of breath or chest pain
Unilateral painful swelling with warmth (possible deep vein thrombosis)
Swelling in pregnancy with headache or high blood pressure

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Foot, leg, and ankle swelling. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Sweating (diaphoresis)
symptoms.description: Diaphoresis is profuse sweating out of proportion to temperature or activity. It accompanies fever and its defervescence, and cold sweats occur with sympathetic activation in acute coronary syndrome, hypoglycemia, shock and pain.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Sweating has many physiological and pathological causes, but diaphoresis with chest pain raises concern for myocardial infarction.
red_flags: Sweating with chest pain or breathlessness
Sweating with confusion or tremor in a person with diabetes (possible hypoglycemia)
Cold, clammy skin with low blood pressure

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Sweating. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Dizziness / lightheadedness
symptoms.description: Dizziness is a term used for two main symptoms: lightheadedness (a feeling of faintness) and vertigo (a false sense of spinning or movement). Lightheadedness often reflects reduced blood flow to the brain, while vertigo usually reflects inner ear or brainstem disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Dizziness is common and arises from cardiovascular, vestibular, metabolic, medication and neurological causes.
red_flags: Slurred speech, double vision, facial droop or limb weakness

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Dizziness. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: One-sided weakness or numbness
symptoms.description: Hemiparesis is weakness of one side of the body, often with numbness (hemisensory loss). Sudden onset is a hallmark of stroke; middle cerebral artery infarction typically causes contralateral weakness and sensory loss affecting the face and arm more than the leg.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Sudden one-sided weakness or numbness is a focal neurological deficit that strongly localises to the brain and points toward stroke.
red_flags: Sudden onset (note the time last known well)

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Lui F, Khan Suheb MZ, Patti L. Ischemic Stroke. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.
Weakness. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Facial droop
symptoms.description: Facial droop is weakness of the facial muscles causing asymmetry of the face, such as a drooping mouth corner. Stroke typically causes lower facial weakness with forehead sparing, whereas Bell's palsy affects the whole side of the face including the forehead.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Sudden facial droop is a highly localising neurological sign and a core feature of stroke recognition tools.
red_flags: Sudden onset with arm or leg weakness

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Lui F, Khan Suheb MZ, Patti L. Ischemic Stroke. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.
Facial paralysis. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Slurred or difficult speech
symptoms.description: Speech difficulty includes dysarthria (slurred, poorly articulated speech from weakness or incoordination of speech muscles) and aphasia (impaired production or comprehension of language from injury to the dominant hemisphere). Sudden onset is a classic warning sign of stroke.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Sudden slurred speech or language disturbance localises to the brain and strongly suggests stroke or transient ischemic attack.

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Lui F, Khan Suheb MZ, Patti L. Ischemic Stroke. In: StatPearls [Internet]. Treasure Island (FL): StatPearls Publishing.
Speech impairment in adults. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Confusion / altered mental status
symptoms.description: Confusion is the inability to think as clearly or quickly as usual, with disorientation and difficulty with attention, memory and decisions. Acute confusion (delirium) is a medical emergency commonly caused by infection, metabolic derangement, hypoxia, drugs or brain disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Acute confusion signals serious illness but arises from many systemic and neurological causes.
red_flags: Low oxygen saturation or low blood pressure

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Confusion. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Sensitivity to light (photophobia)
symptoms.description: Photophobia is discomfort or pain in the eyes in response to bright light. It is a common feature of migraine and also occurs with meningitis, subarachnoid hemorrhage and inflammatory eye disease.
symptoms.weight_rationale: Photophobia with headache favours migraine but is also a feature of meningeal irritation, giving moderate specificity.

references.source_name: Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking
references.citation_text: Bickley LS, Szilagyi PG, Hoffman RM, Soriano RP. Bates' Guide to Physical Examination and History Taking. 13th ed. Philadelphia: Wolters Kluwer; 2021.
Photophobia. MedlinePlus Medical Encyclopedia. Bethesda (MD): U.S. National Library of Medicine.

symptoms.name: Visual aura
symptoms.description: A visual aura is a transient, fully reversible visual disturbance that develops gradually over at least 5 minutes and lasts up to 60 minutes, often preceding migraine headache. It typically begins as a small area of vision loss or bright shimmering lines (scintillating scotoma) that expands across the visual field.
symptoms.weight_rationale: A gradually spreading, positive visual disturbance lasting 5-60 minutes is highly characteristic of migraine with aura.
red_flags: Sudden onset rather than gradual spread
Only negative symptoms (vision loss) without positive phenomena
Accompanying weakness, facial droop or speech difficulty
